game.name: Dead Cells
game.short_description: Dead Cells is a roguelite, metroidvania inspired, action-platformer. You'll explore a sprawling, ever-changing castle... assuming you’re able to fight your way past its keepers in 2D souls-lite combat. No checkpoints. Kill, die, learn, repeat.

commentary.label: Tier list Part 1 (2023)
commentary.summary: Dead Cells is a fast-paced action roguelite where you always play the same character and build each run around the weapons and gear you find. He considers it very popular for good reason, with distinct weapons, great balance and superb game feel. He also praises the developers' constant stream of updates and DLC. He disputes the metroidvania label but still calls it one of the best action roguelikes and places it in S tier.
praise: Every weapon feels distinct, with its own animations and clearly careful design
Excellent balance: almost any weapon is viable for a successful run
Game feel is outstanding; you are fast and feel powerful, cutting through enemies
Each run feels unique even with few passives, since weapons carry the variety
Developers keep releasing updates and DLC, adding bosses, biomes and weapons
Developers published a talk explaining how they designed it to feel good
criticism: Marketed as a metroidvania, which he disagrees with; it is effectively a standard roguelite once the traversal abilities are unlocked
Only three to four hours of ability unlocking gate the world traversal, after which the metroidvania element fades
Few unique passives, so variety relies almost entirely on weapons
unique_points: Variety comes from weapon design rather than passives or differing characters
Weapon animations and feel are individually designed, making each one a different playstyle
Ongoing content updates keep the game fresh for years
commentary.quote: in terms of like action roguelikes it's one of the best it's an easy s tier
comparisons: Metroidvania games (as a genre label he rejects)
design_criteria: Game feel: speed and power fantasy make combat satisfying
Weapon diversity: each weapon has unique animations and behaviour
Balance: nearly all weapons are viable
Run variety: runs feel unique despite few passives
Content updates: ongoing DLC, bosses, biomes and weapons
Genre honesty: metroidvania label seen as marketing rather than design

community.one_liner: A 2D roguelite action-platformer with Metroidvania-style exploration and fast, souls-lite combat, where each run through a procedurally assembled castle ends in permadeath and permanent unlocks.
community.consensus_summary: Dead Cells is one of the most acclaimed roguelites ever made: 97% positive across about 184k Steam reviews (Overwhelmingly Positive), Metacritic 89 and OpenCritic 89 from 150+ critics, plus multiple Best Action/Indie awards in 2018. Players and critics agree the combat feel, movement, art, music and build variety are best in class. Complaints center on the unlock grind, same-y repeat runs, hard-to-read hitboxes and two-hit deaths at high difficulty, and especially the way DLC content is visibly gated inside the base game. It left Early Access in August 2018 and has sold over 10 million copies. Content updates ended with Update 35 'The End is Near' in 2024 after Motion Twin cancelled further Evil Empire work; the game is now in bug-fix-only maintenance, which still draws some community resentment.
best_things: Fluid, responsive combat with very tight controls and animation; often cited as the genre benchmark for game feel
Huge weapon, skill and mutation variety that supports many distinct builds (e.g. crit, brutality, tactics scaling) and run-to-run experimentation
Strong roguelite loop: each death unlocks blueprints, runes, and shortcuts so failure feels like progress
Exploration with rune-gated secret areas and hidden details that reward curiosity, blending Metroidvania ideas into runs
Beautiful, vibrant pixel art with fluid animation, and a well-regarded soundtrack
Boss Cell difficulty tiers (BC 0-5) let players scale challenge and add new enemies and mechanics, giving endgame replay value
Assist Mode lets players tune difficulty without disabling achievements; widely praised as true accessibility
Runs well on low-end hardware and Steam Deck; many free updates and cheap, well-liked DLC (Queen and the Sea, Return to Castlevania)
worst_things: DLC zones, doors and achievements appear inside the base game with buy prompts, which many reviewers see as pushy and as making the base game feel incomplete
Unlock grind: weapons and blueprints must be bought with cells/souls repeatedly across runs, so the grind is seen as the content
Fixed early structure means the first biomes are replayed constantly, so runs feel repetitive despite procedural layouts
Hitbox and move-cancel inconsistencies: weapon visuals larger than actual hit areas, tiny enemy hitboxes, and attack animation lock-in make some deaths feel unfair
Enemies attacking from offscreen or through walls and occasional glitches are reported as cheap damage sources in later difficulties
Weak, sparse narrative and lore that many players find underdeveloped
Some weapons feel weak, gimmicky or are hard to make viable, narrowing the builds that actually work at high difficulty
Controller rebinding limitations and achievement restrictions on some options cited by a few reviewers
Some players find combat floaty and the game simple or shallow in build composition, with rewards for successful runs not satisfying enough to keep grinding
improvements: Less intrusive DLC presentation (or hiding DLC content/prompts for non-owners)
Faster or less repetitive unlock economy so the meta progression feels less like a grind
More variety in early-game biomes and route structure so runs diverge earlier
Clearer, more consistent hitboxes and animation-cancel rules
Better balance for underused weapons and more build-defining synergies at high Boss Cell levels
Deeper story and lore delivery and more bosses (base game has few bosses, per critics)
unique_things: Roguelite and Metroidvania fusion: permanent movement runes open new routes in later runs instead of a fixed world map
No checkpoints, no level-up stats: power comes from picking weapons and three-color scroll upgrades within a run (brutality, tactics, survival)
Player-controlled route choice between biomes each run, with a nonlinear branching castle
Curse mechanic (one hit kills until you clear enough kills) as a voluntary risk-reward system
Originally designed as a 3D project by Motion Twin and reworked into pixel-art 2D, which fans credit for its animation quality
Long post-launch life: five years of free updates, crossovers (Castlevania, Hollow Knight, Hades, etc.) and mobile/console ports
tedious_or_disliked: Repeatedly grinding the same early biomes just to fund blueprint unlocks
Dying at high Boss Cell difficulty to two hits after a long run, where a single mistake wipes the run
Buy prompts for DLC content interrupting fast runs, including timed door challenges
Luck-dependent weapon drops that can leave a run without a workable build
Runs that feel deflating after the early game: ramping back up after each death feels barely worth it to some players
divisive_points: Difficulty: many call it fair and skill-based, while others feel two-hit deaths and Curse make higher tiers frustrating
Grind and repetition: fans feel constant progression, while critics feel the core run structure barely changes after 30+ hours
DLC and monetization: many say DLC is cheap and optional, others feel base game is gated and incomplete
Motion Twin vs Evil Empire after update cancellation: some players negative-review to protest the studio, others defend the decision or praise the game regardless
community.reception_notes: Launched in Steam Early Access in May 2017 and quickly passed 1 million sales; 1.0 launched August 2018 on PC and consoles with very strong reviews and Golden Joystick Best Indie and Game Award wins. Motion Twin later sold over 10 million copies (announced at GDC) helped by 34 free updates and a mobile release; third-party revenue estimates (Steam-only, Boxleiter method) give roughly $178M gross / $52M net. Publishing duties shifted to Evil Empire for live ops from 2019 and they produced the DLC (Rise of the Giants, Bad Seed, Fatal Falls, Queen and the Sea, Return to Castlevania). In 2024 Update 35 'The End is Near' became the last content update; Motion Twin said it wanted to avoid 'more of the same', but co-creator Sebastien Benard publicly called the explanation misleading and pointed to an economic cut in favor of Motion Twin's new game Windblown. Recent Steam reviews show a small wave of protest negatives against Motion Twin and notes that the final update shipped unfinished from beta. Metacritic page cites platforms PC, PS4, Xbox One, Switch, iOS.
